text:
maria.chen: quick question — when someone saves a per-route query and then copies it to a model view, who should be the owner by default? route owner or the user who copied it?

kyle: leaning toward the user who copied it being the owner. keeps intent clear and avoids accidental edits by route teams. :thinking_face:

alex: OK but what about quota and routing implications? saved queries are used to generate telemetry slices, and route owners expect to see only queries they manage. if copiers become owners, admins could see a noisy list.

maria.chen: good point. edgecase: user copies a per-route saved query referencing model_id=redwood/gpt-large and pins it to a model view. the model view is shared org-wide. who should control edits?

sarah: proposal: add two fields on savedqueries API: `owner_type: [user|team|route]` and `origin_scope: [route|model|global]`. default owner when copying = the copier, but if copier chooses "make team-owned" the owner_type flips to team. UI shows small badge: "owner: maria / team: infra".

jamie: +1. also need a quick transfer flow for route owners to claim or archive copies that affect route-level telemetry. maybe a "request ownership" button that pings the route owner.

kyle: implementation note: backend savedquery shape might be: `{"id":"...","scope":"model","owner":"maria","owner_type":"user","origin_route":"/routes/123"}`. keep it simple.

alex: watch out for permission combos: route owners should be able to hide copied queries from their route dashboards even if they don't own them. otherwise they'll surface in per-route analytics and confuse metrics owners.

maria.chen: UX idea — in per-route view, show a small filter: "show only route-owned queries" (default on), with a pill to toggle to "include external". default toggle persists per-user.

sarah: from quota side, queries tied to a route should roll up to that route's sampling and quota. if query is copied to model scope but still references route-specific telemetry, we must preserve rollup. suggest a `rollup_route_id` field that keeps attribution.

deploy-bot: deploy scheduled: feature/queries-ownership-api -> staging at 03:00 UTC.

jamie: question on rollout UX — can we soft-launch behind a feature flag named `savedquery_ownership_v1` and toggle per-org? want to test with a few customers first.

kyle: yes. flag + migration: existing saved queries default to `owner_type: team` and `origin_scope: route` when missing. document the migration script.

maria.chen: tiny UI nit: when cloning in the console modal, add a required dropdown: "Save as" [My query | Team | Route-owned (request approval)]. default = My query. prevents accidental route-ownership.

alex: agree. also audit logs: when ownership changes add an entry so infra/product can trace why a query started affecting dashboards.

sarah: telemetry: add a dimension `saved_query_origin` to our event schema (values: route, model, user_copy). will help evaluate noise.

jamie: ok next steps: 1) kyle to spec API shape and migration 2) sarah to add telemetry dims 3) maria + alex to mock UI modal + per-route filter 4) devops to enable flag in staging for internal orgs.

maria.chen: thanks everyone — i'll drop a short PRD in #product-ship later today and attach mocks. :sparkles:

kyle: i'll post the API sketch in this thread tomorrow.

alex: awesome, ping me if you want a quick UX review.

deploy-bot: staging deploy started: feature/queries-ownership-api @ 03:01 UTC — build 4821

maria.chen: noted — thanks!
